clauses.text:
1 . Any officer of employee of the Gov­
ernment assigned to the Foreign Service 
as a Foreign Service Reserve Officer in 
accordance with section 522 (2) of the 
Foreign Service Act of 1946 who was at 
the time of his assignment an officer or 
employee of the Government serving un­
der a war service indefinite or temporary 
indefinite appointment and who is 
reached in regular order for probational 
appointment from a Civil Service regis­
ter appropriate for filling the position in 
which he was serving at the time of as­
signment or who could, with the approval 
of the head of the agency in which he 
was serving, have been given a competi­
tive status under Civil Service Rule III 
if he had remained in his former position, 
shall be considered as having a competi­
tive status as of the date he is reached 
for probational appointment or classifi­
cation.

2. Any officer or employee of the Gov­
ernment who is appointed, at the request 
of the head of the agency in which he 
was serving, as a Foreign Service Staff 
Officer or employee for a period limited in 
duration to four years or less shall be 
entitled to the same rights with regard 
to acquisitiortof a competitive status as is 
provided by section 1  of this order, and 
any such officer or employee who has, or 
acquires, a competitive status shall be 
entitled to the same rights with regard 
to reinstatement in such agency as a per­
son who is assigned to the Foreign Serv­
ice as a Foreign Service Reserve Officer 
is entitled to receive under the terms of 
section 528 of the Foreign Service Act of

3. Whenever an agency fills a position 
previously occupied by a Foreign Service 
Reserve Officer or a Foreign Service Staff 
Officer or employee entitled to reinstate­
ment in such agency under the provi­
sions of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 
and this order, the appointment, promo­
tion, transfer, or other personnel action 
shall be made on a temporary basis pend­
ing the return of the officer or employee 
in question.

4. The Department of State shall, at 
least two months prior to the completion 
of the service of a Foreign Service Re­
serve Officer, Staff Officer, or employee 
entitled to reinstatement under the pro­
visions of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 
or of this order, notify the officer or em­
ployee and the head of the agency in 
which the officer or employee was serv­
ing immediately prior to his assignment 
to the Foreign Service of the proposed 
termination of assignment in the Foreign 
Service, and such agency shall, prior to 
the termination of assignment in the 
Foreign Service, make arrangements for 
the return to duty of such officer or em­
ployee.

5. A person shall be deemed to have 
waived his rights to reinstatement under 
the terms of section 528 of the Foreign 
Service Act of 1946 and the terms of this 
order if he accepts at the termination of 
his period of service in the Foreign Serv­
ice a position elsewhere than in the Gov­
ernment agency in which he has previ­
ously served or fails to avail himself of 
his right to reinstatement within thirty 
days after the end of his period of service 
in the Foreign Service.

6. The Civil Service Commission is 
authorized, after consultation with the 
Department of State, to prescribe such 
rules and regulations as may be neces­
sary to carry out the provisions of this 
order: Provided, that any changes in 
such rules and regulations made subse­
quent to the appointment or assignment 
of personnel for duty with the Foreign 
Service shall not be effective as to such 
personnel without the prior concurrence 
of the Department of Stated

7. This order shall become effective as 
of September 1, 1947.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, including the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (94 Stat.

1946 (22 U.S.C. 928)” and inserting in lieu thereof, “310 of the Foreign Service 
Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3950)”.

(d) Section l-602(b) is amended by striking out “section 528 of the Foreign 
Service Act of 1946” and inserting in lieu thereof “section 310 of the Foreign 
Service Act of 1980 (22 U.S.C. 3950)”.

reported_material_gaps.specific_authority: EO9932 paragraphs 1-2 incorporate Civil Service Rule III and eligibility tied to the appointment held at original Foreign Service assignment. EO10577 replaces the earlier Civil Service Rules and changes appointment systems; the actual 1950 conversion regulation also changes indefinite appointment categories.

versions.research_rationale: Partial candidate. The complete original establishes six continuing substantive rules, expressly effective as of September 1, 1947, although signed February 27, 1948. Individual four-year appointment eligibility, two-month notice, thirty-day reinstatement and waiver conditions do not set a whole-order calendar sunset. EO12107 expressly substitutes OPM for CSC effective January 1, 1979. EO12292 expressly revokes EO9932 effective February 15, 1981, rather than its February 23 signature date. That establishes termination by the cutoff but does not establish first cessation. The revoker identifies a concrete statutory transition from the incorporated 1946 reinstatement regime to 1980 Act section 310; actual statutory history and continuity are unread. Earlier actual Civil Service Rule III and appointment-system changes also require resolution for the status routes. Named-function searches additionally found narrower overseas-program reinstatement limitations; they are recorded as bounded leads and do not establish a global ending. Accrued competitive status and individual reinstatement rights are not declared invalid. Final search and savings closure are withheld, and provisional no status is unchanged.

reasons: All six original operative spans equal the independent paragraph inventory exactly. Paragraph 7 supplies common activation 1947-09-01, not a seventh continuing command. Individual appointment, notice and waiver periods do not end the whole order.
EO12107 sections 2-101(b) and 2-404 support CSC-to-OPM substitution effective 1979-01-01; no substantive rule termination inferred.

EO12292 sections 10(d) and 11 support formal revocation effective 1981-02-15, distinct from signature 1981-02-23. Original prospective rules are terminated by that upper bound. The candidate does not assert that this is their first cessation or invalidate accrued status/individual rights.

Specific incorporated sections 522(2)/528, their material history, 1980 section 310 and transition/savings remain unresolved. Actual EO10577 and 1950 appointment conversion create concrete status-route questions. All first_end values, whole_order_end and savings_residuals remain null; later_source_search remains empty.
Reproduced named/function search matches all 7,825 manifest bytes and 272 query/file counts. It is only the five stated local roots/globs; current-law numeric machine results remain bounded leads.

Independent supplemental reads found EO9952 paragraph 2 express protection of EO9932 rights, EO12293 administration/pay-conversion authority and current 5 CFR 352 subpart E. These do not contradict the partial dates or resolve the retained statutory/accrued-rights gaps.
reviews.scope: Six original substantive rules, express activation, OPM substitution, formal revocation upper bound, retained first-end/statutory/status-route/savings gaps. No full-readiness certification.
